name: maybe_Ui_Tween_EvalModeC7Only
summary: Slot 12 of the evaluator table. Reads the record type byte at +0xC: when it is 7 the keyframe value is sampled (0x325BDC) and the record's offset f_0 is added; for every other type it returns the offset f_0 alone. Real body from the disassembly: ldrb +0xC, vldrne s0,[r4] on mismatch, vadd on match. This is a slot of the 72-entry parameter-evaluator table at 0x7286A0 (copied per instance by 0x326564; dispatched by 0x326428, which tail-calls the slot named by a parameter record's +0x28 id after checking its +0x29 kind byte).
evidence: New: 0x326428 (dispatcher) and 0x326564 (table copy) were found and read; all nine dispatcher callers are text-layout row builders (Text_Layout_BuildDefaultRows 0x48AAE8, Text_RowHasNewline 0x48AC14, ...) plus the shop-price clamp at 0x3C2E00, so this is a layout-parameter evaluator, not a tween player. The readable C dropped the vldrne/vadd tail: on a type mismatch the result is the record's f_0, it is not 'no evaluation'.

name: Os_LogDebugString
summary: Hands the text stored in a debug-string record to the engine log: formats s->f_8 straight into the log object's 0x80-byte message buffer (0x7AC834->+0x848), resets the write pointer, then compacts the record (memmove the 0x20-byte payload at +0xC over the header at +4, clear the +0x24 count) and returns the previous +4 value.
evidence: New: the callee 0x707C1C was disassembled - it is a fixed-size log formatter (push r0-r3, vsnprintf(buf+4, 0x80, fmt=arg2, ap), pop) and this function passes s->f_8 as that format, so this really is 'emit this record's string to the log'. Returns a value (the saved f_4), so a predicate name would be wrong; the body is undamaged.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateReelTimer
summary: Slot-machine frame timer: increments the frame counter at +0x600 and, on every exact multiple of 5, runs one step of the stop sequence - steps 5..10 call 0x4C2C60(self->f_10, 5..0) with a descending argument, step 11 copies the final float pair from the global 0x72ABF8+0x18 into self+0x18.
evidence: New: this address is entry 0x0072AC08 of the slot-window method table, whose neighbours are now named (Ui_SlotWindow_ProcessPatterns 0x327D20, Ui_SlotWindow_ResetPayoutAnim 0x328E58, Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackE 0x327EC8), so the 'Casino_Slot' prefix was invented; the divisor/remainder idiom is a /5 frame tick and the switch is the 5..0 countdown.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateSubWidget

name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateChildSelection

evidence: New: the counterpart 0x316994 is now confidently named maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetRecordHandle and its body is byte-for-byte the same guarded handle test, so this is the dive-start window's version of the same setter; only the store offset (+0x284) and the object (+0x2d4) differ.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveResultWindow_ShowItem

evidence: New: the body's callees are now named - Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow, Text_SetCommandArgs, Text_ExecuteCommand - so this is not a 3D model display but a text command that renders the item (icon/name) of a list row; the neighbours are the Ui_Dive* windows (0x32BD88, 0x32C33C, 0x32C91C), hence the dive-result-window prefix.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveResultWindow_Update

evidence: New: the condition helper is now named maybe_Script_MessageConditionCheckC, and the release pattern (vtable+8 then clear the matching flag byte) matches the other UI destructors; the body is still partly damaged (self[2]/self[5] array indexing lost its types), so the name stays a maybe.

name: Ui_DiveManager_DeletingDtor

evidence: New: the plain destructor 0x32C92C is now named maybe_Ui_DiveManager_Dtor, and this address is exactly 'dtor(); 0x10F6CC();' - the standard deleting-destructor shape used by every other named deleting dtor in the binary (e.g. the scene-object one). 'Destroy' hid that it is the delete variant.

It is a fragment of that function, not a separate one.
